## Did You Know?
Vice President Rockefeller...
*   ...had both business and public-service experience.  
*   ...ran for the office of President three times (1960, 1964, & 1968).  
*   ...didn't run for Vice-President, but was appointed to the office and had to be conformed by the Senate.  
*   ...died under mysterious circumstances.

## Biography
Nelson Aldrich Rockefeller was an American businessman and politician who served as the 41st vice president of the United States from 1974 to 1977, and previously as the 49th governor of New York from 1959 to 1973. He also served as assistant secretary of State for American Republic Affairs for Presidents Franklin D. Roosevelt and Harry S. Truman (1944–1945) as well as under secretary of Health, Education and Welfare under Dwight D. Eisenhower from 1953 to 1954. A grandson of billionaire John D. Rockefeller and a member of the wealthy Rockefeller family, he was a noted art collector and served as administrator of Rockefeller Center in Manhattan, New York City.

## Quotes
> “Wherever we look upon this earth, the opportunities take shape within the problems.”
—Nelson Rockefeller
> “I do not believe it right for one group to impose its vision of morality on an entire society.”
—Nelson Rockefeller

**Hannibal Hamlin** (August 27, 1809 – July 4, 1891) was an American politician and diplomat who was the 15th [vice president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States"), serving from 1861 to 1865, during President [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln")'s first term. He was the first [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") vice president.
texts.4: As an attorney from [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine"), Hamlin began his political career as a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") in the Maine House of Representatives before being elected twice to the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives"), and then to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). With his strong [abolitionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionist "Abolitionist") views, he left the Democratic Party for the newly formed Republican Party in 1856. In the [1860 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election "1860 United States presidential election"), Hamlin balanced the successful Republican ticket as a New Englander partnered with the Midwesterner Lincoln. ## Biography
Nelson Aldrich Rockefeller was an American businessman and politician who served as the 41st vice president of the United States from 1974 to 1977, and previously as the 49th governor of New York from 1959 to 1973. He also served as assistant secretary of State for American Republic Affairs for Presidents Franklin D. Roosevelt and Harry S. Truman (1944–1945) as well as under secretary of Health, Education and Welfare under Dwight D. Eisenhower from 1953 to 1954. A grandson of billionaire John D. Rockefeller and a member of the wealthy Rockefeller family, he was a noted art collector and served as administrator of Rockefeller Center in Manhattan, New York City.
